plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and you pay only the second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're the highest). Bidding above or below true value only risks either winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Since this is a one-shot round with no repeated interaction to exploit collusion, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction, which is strategically similar to a Vickrey auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below my value, I reduce my chances of winning without any benefit, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $8.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (bid = value) is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, my optimal strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $44.
